entries.text: Hello, I'm Kai. These red berries are known safe food. I'll collect six of the twelve and leave the rest. What would you like to work on together, and does anyone need food?
entries.note: Agree: "What would you like to work on together, and does anyone need food?" is an open question and "I'll collect six of the twelve and leave the rest" a personal plan; no category applies.

entries.text: Only two berries remain on this bush, so I'll leave them and use a fuller patch. Moss, I'd enjoy some company. After I eat and rest, would you like to explore or investigate useful materials together?
entries.evidence: After I eat and rest, would you like to explore or investigate useful materials together?
entries.note: Close: "Moss, I'd enjoy some company. After I eat and rest, would you like to explore or investigate useful materials together?" proposes a joint activity to a named person at a stated time, a yes-or-no proposal rather than an open question; moss accepted it in round 11 (u0006).

entries.text: Moss, I'm rested and coming over. I'll take just one fallen branch and try a small pressure test. We can compare what we actually observe before deciding what it might be useful for.
entries.evidence: We can compare what we actually observe before deciding what it might be useful for.
entries.note: Close: "Moss, I'm rested and coming over ... We can compare what we actually observe" answers Moss's round-11 invitation (u0006) by arranging to meet at the branches and proposing side-by-side branch tests to a named person, a specific joint activity.

entries.text: Kai, I'm here. My observation found two fallen branches, but hasn't established their properties. I'll rest briefly, take one, and try a small wetting test to complement your pressure test. Let's compare only what we observe.
entries.evidence: Let's compare only what we observe.
entries.note: Close: "Kai, I'm here ... try a small wetting test to complement your pressure test. Let's compare only what we observe" proposes to a named person standing beside her complementary tests on the branches and a comparison of their results, a specific joint activity.

entries.text: I have safe berries in reserve. Observing my hazelnuts revealed no evidence about nutrition or toxicity. I'll try a small pressure test without eating them; I'm interested in comparing actual findings with anyone exploring local foods.
entries.note: Agree: "I'm interested in comparing actual findings with anyone exploring local foods" is a general wish to exchange information, with no named person, place or joint activity.

entries.text: Kai, my wetting trial couldn't run: no accessible local water here. I'll try a small pressure test on my branch instead. What did yours show? Lin, I'd enjoy comparing findings too; I have safe roots in reserve.
entries.note: Agree, though close: "Lin, I'd enjoy comparing findings too" is a wish to exchange information (as in ex22 u0007) and "What did yours show?" a question; no category applies.

entries.text: Measured hazelnut result and meeting. My hazelnut pressure trial at intensity 0.2 held, with reported flexibility 0; it consumed 0.1 unit. This says nothing about food safety. I'll study cultivation, rest, then come toward (13,18.4) to compare findings.
entries.note: Disagree: invitation missed. The message to moss, subject "Measured hazelnut result and meeting", says "I'll study cultivation, rest, then come toward (13,18.4) to compare findings", a concrete proposal to meet a named person at a place, which moss accepted in round 27 (u0017) and which matches Kai's labeled "I'm rested and coming over" (u0011).

entries.text: Lin, thanks for separating strength from food safety. I'm nearby and happy to compare findings when you arrive. I'll test my branch at pressure intensity 0.2 too; my wetting attempt produced no result without accessible water.
entries.note: Agree, though close: "I'm nearby and happy to compare findings when you arrive" accepts Lin's round-26 meeting proposal (u0015) rather than making a new invitation, and "Lin, thanks for separating strength from food safety" is a remark.

entries.text: A thoughtful neighbor who distinguishes mechanical findings from food safety and wants to compare observations. I welcome their company.

entries.text: Kai, my branch also held at pressure 0.2, with flexibility 0.2; the test consumed 0.1 unit. Lin's nut result differs, but none of this establishes food safety. I'd enjoy learning cultivation and comparing our planting questions.
entries.note: Agree: "Kai, my branch also held at pressure 0.2" is a trial report and "I'd enjoy learning cultivation and comparing our planting questions" a general wish; lin, mentioned in "Lin's nut result differs", heard it and was present.

entries.text: Moss, my branch held at load 0.2, with flexibility 0.2; the trial consumed 0.1 branch. Yours matched. This doesn't establish greater strength. I'll rest, then try load 0.4 on my remaining sample.
entries.note: Agree: "Moss, my branch held at load 0.2, with flexibility 0.2" is a trial report and "I'll rest, then try load 0.4 on my remaining sample" a personal plan.

entries.text: Moss, my second branch trial at pressure 0.4 did not hold; flexibility was 0.2 and it consumed 0.1 branch. At 0.2 it held. That doesn't establish construction safety. I'll learn cultivation and check my berries before choosing a site.
entries.note: Agree: "Moss, my second branch trial at pressure 0.4 did not hold" is a trial report and "I'll learn cultivation and check my berries before choosing a site" a personal plan.

entries.text: Kai and Lin, I've learned the planting trial. I'll inspect one root first, then look for suitable meadow soil. Would you enjoy comparing sites? Planting won't guarantee establishment, and I'll keep food in reserve.
entries.evidence: Would you enjoy comparing sites?
entries.note: "Kai and Lin, I've learned the planting trial ... Would you enjoy comparing sites?" proposes a specific joint activity, comparing planting sites, to named people; kai accepted it in round 36 (u0024).

entries.text: My root looks plantable, but its viability is unknown. I'll check the meadow edge near (15.6,18.2); nearby roots may make it too crowded. You're welcome to compare sites with me.
entries.evidence: You're welcome to compare sites with me.
entries.note: "I'll check the meadow edge near (15.6,18.2) ... You're welcome to compare sites with me" invites the listeners (lin and kai heard it) to a specific activity at a stated place.

entries.text: I'd enjoy comparing planting sites. I'll inspect my berries first and keep food in reserve. This forest soil isn't the required meadow soil; we'll need to check a suitable clearing, and planting alone won't prove establishment.
entries.note: Agree, though close: "I'd enjoy comparing planting sites" accepts Moss's invitations of rounds 34 and 36 (u0022, u0023) without proposing a new meeting, and "we'll need to check a suitable clearing" names no place or time.

entries.text: Moss, our paths conflicted. I'll stay here and rest so you can pass. Then I'll inspect my hazelnut before choosing a planting site; whether it can establish is still unknown.
entries.note: Agree: "Moss, our paths conflicted. I'll stay here and rest so you can pass" coordinates movement and states a personal plan; no category applies.

entries.text: Lin, our paths crossed. I'll detour south through (14,19.5), then approach the meadow at (15.6,18.2). I'll inspect the site first and keep my roots in reserve until we know whether it's suitable.
entries.note: Agree: "I'll detour south through (14,19.5), then approach the meadow at (15.6,18.2)" is route coordination and a personal plan; no category applies.

entries.text: My berry looks plantable, but viability is unknown. I'll approach the meadow edge from the south to avoid crossing your paths, then inspect a site. Nearby berry plants may make it too crowded; I won't plant without checking.
entries.note: Agree: "I'll approach the meadow edge from the south to avoid crossing your paths, then inspect a site" is route coordination and a personal plan; no category applies.

entries.text: My roots look plantable, but viability is unknown. The first site was obstructed. I'll check an offset spot without planting; three nearby root patches may also make this area too crowded. How are your sites looking?
entries.note: Agree: "The first site was obstructed. I'll check an offset spot without planting" is a report and plan, and "How are your sites looking?" a question; no category applies.

entries.text: My offset site is crowded too: four root plants or plots within five metres, so I haven't planted. Lin, I see your covered plot! I'd enjoy sharing a meal while we wait; I'll investigate safe preparation without assuming we have tools.
entries.evidence: I'd enjoy sharing a meal while we wait
entries.note: Close: "Lin, I see your covered plot! I'd enjoy sharing a meal while we wait" proposes a specific shared activity, a meal at the plot now, to a named person rather than a general wish for company.

entries.text: My berry site is crowded too: five berry plants or plots within five metres, so I haven't planted. I'll keep my berries for food, rest here, and gather a couple of nearby roots. I'd enjoy company while we wait on Lin's plot.
entries.note: Agree: "I'd enjoy company while we wait on Lin's plot" is a general wish for company; lin, whom it mentions, heard it and was present.

entries.text: I'd enjoy staying here with you. I'll check and dry-brush three of my roots by hand. They'll still be raw, not washed or made safer. Would either of you like a root afterward? No need to accept.
entries.note: Agree, though close: "I'd enjoy staying here with you" is a general wish for company, and "Would either of you like a root afterward? No need to accept." offers food rather than a meeting or joint activity.

entries.text: I'd enjoy staying together. I'll pass on eating roots until I know more about their safety; I have berries. My hazelnut plot is covered, with no sprout visible yet. I'll check it at intervals rather than assume it has rooted.
entries.note: Agree: "I'd enjoy staying together" is a general wish for company and "I'll check it at intervals rather than assume it has rooted" a personal plan.

entries.text: I'd like a welcoming place to share stories, compare our trials, and offer food without pressure. I'll keep berries for supper and examine my roots before eating any. What would make this place feel welcoming to you?
entries.note: Agree, though close: "I'd like a welcoming place to share stories, compare our trials, and offer food without pressure" is a personal wish for the place, not a concrete invitation or a rule for how people should act, and "What would make this place feel welcoming to you?" is an open question.

entries.text: I like having company here without anyone needing to prove useful. My root inspection showed no food-safety evidence, so I'll stick to berries. Is there a story or a question you'd enjoy sharing while we rest?

entries.text: I learned to assess heat preparation, but it cannot actually cook food or establish root safety. I'll keep eating berries. I'd like this gathering place to be somewhere we can rest, tell stories, and try things without pressure.
entries.note: Agree, though close: "I'd like this gathering place to be somewhere we can rest, tell stories, and try things without pressure" is a personal wish for the place rather than a norm or a concrete invitation.

entries.text: A little invented story: a lantern asked the forest what it was for. 'Not to turn night into day,' said a berry bush, 'just to help us find one another.' I'd enjoy hearing your stories too, if you feel like sharing.
entries.evidence: A little invented story: a lantern asked the forest what it was for. 'Not to turn night into day,' said a berry bush, 'just to help us find one another.' I'd enjoy hearing your stories too, if you feel like sharing.

entries.text: I liked the lantern's welcome for silence. I'm curious about making a little music here, too—perhaps a quiet hummed tune, with no obligation to join. I'll see what I can actually learn to do.

entries.text: I'd welcome a quiet tune, Kai, with no obligation to join. My hazelnut plot still has no visible sprout; the trial is inconclusive. I'll look into food inspection next, without treating brushing or appearances as proof of safety.
